title: motion-strip re-implements run_demo's driver (~70 lines) and its documented drift safety net does not exist
evidence: harness/motion_strip.odin:60-77: '// run setup — the SAME pieces run_demo applies (fixture + nodes + spawns' / '// + session + growth + era), so the strip's sim timeline is the blessed' / '// one (the T1 manifest pins it; this verb just renders it).' then 'pp.run_init(&state, demo.seed, cat.hash, cat.balance.logic_hz)' / 'state.era = demo.era' / 'cfg := Demo_Replay{ name = demo_name, use_fixture = demo.use_fixture, qos_fixture = demo.qos_fixture, growth_on = demo.growth_on, advance_gate_on = demo.advance_gate_on, session = {goal = demo.win_goal, cap_ms = demo.lose_cap_ms, health_on = demo.health_on, surge_win_pct = demo.surge_win_pct}, }' — a verbatim copy of harness/run.odin:291-303 ('cfg := Demo_Replay{ name = demo.name, use_fixture = demo.use_fixture, ... advance_gate_on = demo.advance_gate_on, // 6.2: run setup — the era-advance gate (r1 B1: ...)'), plus the copied per-tick loop ('for cmd in state.action_log { if cmd.apply_tick == sim_tick {' + 'pp.step(&state, sim_tick, batch[:], cat)'). grep 'state_hash' harness/motion_strip.odin → 0 matches. Drift precedent, harness/overlay.odin:50: 'advance_gate_on = d.advance_gate_on, // 6.2 r2 W2: the B1 flag-threading's residual site — the overlay verb re-sims the gate demos gate-ON too, or its verification frame shows the wrong sim'. PR body (_bmad-output/pr-bodies/v2-motion-readability.md:93-94) claims: 'so a drift in the strip driver would fail `harness run` (the blessed manifest) before it could mislead a measurement.'
detail: harness run exercises run_demo's driver, not the strip's copy — the strip never hashes, so strip-driver drift cannot fail anything and would silently mislead evidence. The overlay copy already missed a flag once.
recommended_fix: Extract the shared boot+step into one helper used by run_demo/overlay/motion_strip, or have motion-strip compare pp.state_hash against the blessed .t1 while rendering.

title: README holds metric (21/24, 10/24) cannot be produced by the shipped tool (lost≠hold hardening not reflected)
evidence: README.md:33: '| holds (<0.5px/frame) | 21 of 24 | 10 of 24 (post-arrival) |' — but tools/measure_packet_motion.py:60: 'disp = None  # lost track — never a hold' and the count excludes lost frames: 'b_holds = sum(1 for _, d in before if d is not None and d < 0.5)'. Running the README's own reproduce commands on this tree prints: 'holds (<0.5px): BEFORE=9/24  AFTER=1/24' and 'lost track (packet absent): BEFORE=12  AFTER=9' (9+12=21, 1+9=10 — the README numbers fold lost frames into holds, the pre-r1 tool semantics).
detail: The r1-hardened tool separates lost from holds but the README/PR summary table was never regenerated; a reviewer reproducing the evidence gets different headline numbers than documented.
recommended_fix: Regenerate the summary table from the shipped tool (report holds and lost separately), or footnote that 21/24 predates the lost≠hold hardening.

title: README reproduce block says 46 demos green; this tree has 47 and runs 47
evidence: README.md:87: 'tools/harness.sh run                       # 46 demos green (T1+T2+replay)' — the tree contains 47 demos (ls demos/*.dem | wc -l → 47; the #80 estate-spawning rebase merged additional demos) and ./bin/harness run on this tree prints 'harness: 47 demo(s) green'.
detail: Stale count from before the final rebase; a reviewer running the reproduce step sees 47 and wonders what changed.
recommended_fix: Update the count to 47 (or drop the hardcoded number from the reproduce block).

title: Trail echoes multiply RGB as well as alpha, contradicting the 'packet's own body color at low alpha' comment and the file's alpha-only dim idiom
evidence: view.odin:1573 (the stated intent): '// packet: the packet's own body color at low alpha, oldest first,'. view.odin:1584-1585 (the code): 'ebody := rl.Color{u8(f32(body.r) * fade), u8(f32(body.g) * fade), u8(f32(body.b) * fade), u8(f32(body.a) * fade)}' / 'eout := rl.Color{u8(f32(outline.r) * fade), u8(f32(outline.g) * fade), u8(f32(outline.b) * fade), u8(f32(outline.a) * fade)}'. The file's existing dim idiom, view.odin:1568-1569 (focus ghost), is alpha-only: 'body.a = u8(f32(body.a) * 0.22)' / 'outline.a = u8(f32(outline.a) * 0.22)'.
detail: With alpha-blended fills (field notes confirm rlsw blends filled circles), RGB×fade plus A×fade gives fade-squared visibility (~9% for the 0.30 echo) — a darker color, not the spec's 'packet color at low alpha'.
recommended_fix: Either multiply alpha only (spec-literal; re-verify the Kyle crops) or fix the comment to state the deliberate double-fade.
